item.title: Manchester City v Arsenal: Women’s Super League – live
item.description:

GOAL! West Ham 0-2 Chelsea (Walsh 80) An emphatic finish from Keira Walsh has clinched all three points for Chelsea.

Beth Mead starts against her old club, one of three changes to the City side that drew with Real Madrid in midweek. Sam Coffey and Niamh Charles also come into the team, Charles for her first City start. Out go Laura Brown, Mary Fowler and Kerstin Casparij.

item.title: ‘Insane’: F1 drivers unite over engine regulations after chaotic Bahrain GP
item.description:
• Antonelli and Hamilton led the criticism in Sepang

  • Race delayed for 53 minutes after software problems

Formula One’s drivers issued a damning condemnation of the sport’s current engine regulations that caused the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia to open with farcical scenes of cars stopping on track and unable to accelerate because of software problems in the electronics that control the engines.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won in Sepang but only after F1 suffered the embarrassment of a host of cars barely able to complete two formation laps in the wet as they were making their way to the grid.

item.title: Djokovic rolls back years to beat Zverev in thriller as Sabalenka swept out in China
item.description:
• Serb into China Open semis after 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 win

  • Sabalenka loses to 34th-ranked Bartunkova

Novak Djokovic rolled back the years to oust Alexander Zverev from the China Open on Sunday, beating the top seed 4-6, 6-4, 6-4 to set up a blockbuster semi-final with Daniil Medvedev.

The 39-year-old Serbian electrified a packed crowd in Beijing, where he extended an astonishing winning streak to 32 matches and is a firm fan favourite. He got off to a poor start, double-faulting twice in the first game to help Zverev, a decade his junior, break serve instantly.

item.title: Daryz wins back-to-back Prix de l’Arc de Triomphes at Longchamp – as it happened
item.description:
• Daryz pips Bay City Roller to victory in Paris

Social media reports suggest that Spirit Tango, who ran in the first race at ParisLongchamp today, has had to be put down. A very sad postscript to the Prix Marcel Boussac and news which follows the death of another horse on Arc weekend after the demise of another British runner in Fallen Angel on Saturday.

Green Empress provided trainer Joseph O’Brien with another big-race success in a stellar year when narrowly holding off Data to win the Prix Marcel Boussac, the forst race at ParisLongchamp on Arc day.
